name: Caltech 101: 101 Object Categories
description: Caltech 101 consists of pictures of objects belonging to 101 distinct categories, plus an additional background clutter category, containing a total of 9,145 images. Each category contains roughly 40 to 800 images, commonly sized around 300x200 pixels. Created at the California Institute of Technology by Fei-Fei Li, Marco Andreetto, and Marc'Aurelio Ranzato in 2004, it is a foundational early object recognition benchmark.

citation.paper_title: Learning Generative Visual Models from Few Training Examples: An Incremental Bayesian Approach Tested on 101 Object Categories

provenance.collection_method: Images collected from Google Image Search in 2003 and subsequently manually pruned to retain canonical object viewpoints.
provenance.curation_notes: Objects are predominantly centered and oriented upright with minimal background occlusion.
